texte:
The Clock Goes Toc Toc!
Workshop au 32Bis

📅 2, 16 et 23 décembre 2026 & 16 janvier 2027
🕒 De 14h30 à 16h
👥 À partir de 8 ans, sans limite d’âge
✨ Gratuit, sur inscription via le formulaire en ligne (lien en bio).

En écho au numéro de The Funambulist, 'They Have Clocks, We Have Time', cet atelier, imaginé et animé par l’artiste Sarah Nefissa Belhadjali, propose d’explorer différentes manières de mesurer et d’habiter le temps.

Il débutera par un temps de découverte et d’étude de références d’horloges conçues ou détournées par des artistes, afin d’interroger notre rapport aux instruments de mesure du temps et aux normes qu’ils véhiculent.

Les participant·es seront ensuite invité·es à imaginer et fabriquer leur propre horloge fictive, en reprenant les codes d’une horloge classique ou en inventant une forme entièrement nouvelle. 

À propos
Sarah Nefissa Belhadjali est une artiste italo-franco-tunisienne, diplômée des Beaux-Arts de Paris. Sa pratique explore les relations entre art, institutions et dispositifs de visibilité, à travers des approches performatives, curatoriales et pédagogiques.

-----

Workshop
The Clock Goes Toc Toc!

📅 December 2, 16 and 23, 2026, and January 16, 2027.
🕒2:30–4 PM.
👥 Open to everyone aged 8 and over, with no upper age limit.
✨Free admission, registration required via the online form.

In response to The Funambulist issue 'They Have Clocks, We Have Time', this workshop, conceived and led by artist Sarah Nefissa Belhadjali, invites participants to explore different ways of measuring and experiencing time.

It begins with an introduction and exploration of clocks designed or reimagined by artists, prompting participants to question their relationship with timekeeping instruments and the norms they convey.

Participants will then be invited to imagine and create their own fictional clock, either reinterpreting the codes of a traditional clock or inventing an entirely new form.

About
Sarah Nefissa Belhadjali is an Tunisian-Italian-French artist and a graduate of the École des Beaux-Arts de Paris. Her practice explores the relationships between art, institutions and the ways in which artistic practices are made visible,

texte:
A big thank you to everyone who came to visit 'Kids of the World, Unite!', an exhibition celebrating 10 years of The Funambulist Magazine.

Our special thanks go to Shivangi Mariam Raj for presenting the exhibition and sharing insights into the magazine's work and archive, and to artists Mouna Karray and Nidhal Chamekh for accepting our invitation to take part in this exhibition and bring their work into dialogue with The Funambulist.

The exhibition remains open to the public until January 15, 2027. We look forward to welcoming you at 32Bis!

Opening hours:
Tuesday to Sunday · 11am–6pm

Photo credit: @mehdi.ben.temessek

Designed as an invitation to participate, this exhibition seeks to think equally with our children as well as our elders, contemplating the material conditions of the production and circulation of knowledge. It invites us to envision the collective consciousness we can develop together by expanding our conception of the classroom.

The exhibition opens at 32bis, Rue Ben Gedhahem, Tunis (third floor) on November 6, 2026, at 5:00 PM and will be on view till January 15, 2027. 

All are welcome to join!

texte:
On the occasion of its 10th anniversary, The Funambulist is welcomed by 32Bis from November 6, 2026, to January 15, 2027, to reflect on collective forms, methods, and strategies for building our liberation pedagogies.

Thinking equally with our children as well as our elders, this intervention focuses on shared learning. It features a reading room with access to all the issues of the magazine spanning over a decade, dedicated listening corners for some of their podcast episodes, an exhibition, a conversation on nourishing international solidarities, and workshops for children, young adults, and publishing enthusiasts.

//

The Funambulist is a bilingual print and online magazine that engages with the politics of space and bodies. From 2015 onwards, the magazine has operated at the crossroads of architecture, academia, and activism by formulating spatial approaches to struggles around the world.

32Bis is a contemporary art center nestled in the heart of downtown Tunis. Its mission is to promote both Tunisian and international artists, offering a perspective on artistic scenes from the Global South. Through exhibitions, conferences, artistic residencies, and its media library dedicated to visual arts, 32Bis fosters artistic creation, research, and exchange.

More details to follow soon!

Poster image: Details from Exil I (2019) by Nidhal Chamekh.
Photo: Daniele Molajoli.

في إطار الاحتفال بعشريتها، يستضيف 32 بيس من 6 نوفمبر 2026 إلى 15 جانفي 2027 ، مجلة The Funambulist ،
للتفكيرمعا في الأشكال والمناهج والاستراتيجيات الجماعية لمناهجنا التربوية.
على قدم المساواة مع أطفالنا وكبارنا على حد سواء، يركز هذا المشروع على التعلم المشترك، يتضمن  قاعة قراءة تتيح الاطلاع على الأعداد الكاملة للمجلة ، الذي يمتد لأكثر من عقد من الزمن، وركن انصات مخصص للاستماع إلى بعض حلقات البودكاست الخاصة بها، ومعرضًا يضم أعمالا بصرية وخرائطية من صفحاتها، وحوارًا حول تعزيز التضامن، وورشات عمل مخصصة للأطفال والشباب وهواة النشر.

The Funambulist هي مجلة ورقية وإلكترونية ثنائية اللغة، تتناول سياسات الفضاء والأجساد. ومنذ عام 2015، تعمل المجلة على تقاطع العمارة والأوساط الأكاديمية والنشاط، من خلال صياغة مقاربات فضائية للنضالات.

32 بيس هو مركز فني معاصر يقع في قلب وسط مدينة تونس. يسعى إلى دعم الفنا
